tempo.basis: from five complete recordings, median 1:39 (Wunderlich/Giesen 1:33, Güra/Schultsz 1:38, Fischer-Dieskau/Höll 1:39, Grahl/Heide 1:41, Maltman/Johnson 1:42), 1.5 s allowed for silence; 26 bars of 2/4 and a sixteenth-note pickup = about 52 quarter notes, no repeats; Schumann marks it Langsam, zart

phrases: In the wondrously beautiful month of May, when all the buds burst open,
ɪm ˈvʊndərʃøːnən ˈmoːnat maɪ als ˈalə ˈknɔspən ˈʃpraŋən
then love rose up in my heart.
daː ɪst ɪn ˈmaɪnəm ˈhɛrtsən diː ˈliːbə ˈaʊfɡəɡaŋən
In the wondrously beautiful month of May, when all the birds were singing,
ɪm ˈvʊndərʃøːnən ˈmoːnat maɪ als ˈalə ˈføːɡəl ˈzaŋən
then I confessed to her my longing and desire.
daː haːp ɪç iːr ɡəˈʃtandən maɪn ˈzeːnən ʊnt fɛrˈlaŋən

facts.key: F-sharp minor / A major (three sharps), ending unresolved on a dominant seventh

notes: Words by Heinrich Heine (Lyrisches Intermezzo, 1822-23). IPA follows sung German (Bühnenaussprache): r rolled or flipped, final -er as [ər], ch after front vowels [ç], after back vowels [x]. Literal translation, for meaning.
